sections.preamble: You answer questions about a single medical image. Follow the answer format requested in the user message exactly.

content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a soft-tissue mass.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

The brightest, most mass-like area is the hyperintense lesion at left-center, around x=270, y=380 in the left panel. In the right panel, offset by 784 px, that corresponds to about x=1054, y=380.

Marks near this region:
- Mark 25 is at (1024, 368), toward the right edge of the lesion.
- Mark 13 is at (1067, 393), well within the bright area.

The lesion spans roughly x=225–310 and y=345–420 in the left panel, which is x=1009–1094 in the right panel. Its center is therefore near (1050, 385). Mark 13 at (1067, 393) is about 17 px from that center. Mark 25 at (1024, 368) is about 31 px away, near the edge where a dark cystic or air spot sits.

Mark 13 is the closest to the center.

ANSWER: 13
